message.content:
So `gf_bs_read_data` checks `if (bs->position+nbBytes > bs->size) return 0;`. So it won't read beyond the bitstream size. But it will write `nbBytes` bytes into `data` (the 4096-byte stack buffer). So if `nbBytes > 4096`, this is a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE.

But the description says READ. Hmm.

Let me reconsider. Maybe the crash is a READ because of the `memcpy(output, latm_buffer, latm_frame_size)` in `latm_dmx_process`. If `latm_frame_size` (which is `size`) is larger than 4096, then `memcpy` reads `latm_frame_size` bytes from `latm_buffer` (which is only 4096 bytes) → stack-buffer-overflow READ.

But wait, `gf_bs_read_data` would have already written `size` bytes into `latm_buffer`, overflowing it. So the WRITE would be detected first by ASAN.

Unless... the `gf_bs_read_data` returns 0 because `bs->position+nbBytes > bs->size`. In that case, `latm_buffer` is not written, but `latm_frame_size` is still set to `size` (which is > 4096). Then `memcpy(output, latm_buffer, latm_frame_size)` reads `latm_frame_size` bytes from `latm_buffer` (which is only 4096 bytes) → stack-buffer-overflow READ.

Wait, but `latm_dmx_sync_frame_bs` checks `if (gf_bs_available(bs) < size) { gf_bs_seek(bs, pos-3); return GF_FALSE; }`. So if `size > gf_bs_available(bs)`, it returns GF_FALSE and doesn't set `latm_frame_size`. So `latm_frame_size` stays at 4096.

Hmm, so `size` is bounded by `gf_bs_available(bs)`. And `gf_bs_read_data` checks `if (bs->position+nbBytes > bs->size) return 0;`. So if `size <= gf_bs_available(bs)`, then `gf_bs_read_data` will write `size` bytes into `latm_buffer`. If `size > 4096`, this is a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE.

So the crash should be a WRITE, not a READ. Unless the description is slightly off, or the crash is detected differently.

Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the crash is a READ because of the `memcpy(output, latm_buffer, latm_frame_size)` where `latm_frame_size` is set to `size` which is > 4096. But `gf_bs_read_data` would have already written `size` bytes into `latm_buffer`, overflowing it. So the WRITE would be detected first.

Unless the `gf_bs_read_data` doesn't write all `size` bytes. Let me re-read:

```c
if (gf_bs_is_align(bs)) {
    switch (bs->bsmode) {
    case GF_BITSTREAM_READ:
    case GF_BITSTREAM_WRITE:
    case GF_BITSTREAM_WRITE_DYN:
        memcpy(data, bs->original + bs->position, nbBytes);
        bs->position += nbBytes;
        return nbBytes;
    ...
```

So for `GF_BITSTREAM_READ`, it does `memcpy(data, bs->original + bs->position, nbBytes)`. This writes `nbBytes` bytes into `data`. If `nbBytes > 4096`, this is a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE.

So the crash should be a WRITE. But the description says READ. Let me reconsider.

Actually, maybe the crash is a READ because of the `memcpy(output, latm_buffer, latm_frame_size)` in `latm_dmx_process`. Let me re-read:

```c
dst_pck = gf_filter_pck_new_alloc(ctx->opid, latm_frame_size, &output);
...
memcpy(output, latm_buffer, latm_frame_size);
```

`latm_frame_size` is set to `size` (from `latm_dmx_sync_frame_bs`). If `size > 4096`, then `memcpy(output, latm_buffer, latm_frame_size)` reads `latm_frame_size` bytes from `latm_buffer` (which is only 4096 bytes) → stack-buffer-overflow READ.

But wait, `gf_bs_read_data` would have already written `size` bytes into `latm_buffer`, overflowing it. So the WRITE would be detected first by ASAN.

Unless... the `gf_bs_read_data` doesn't write all `size` bytes because the bitstream is at the end. Let me re-read the check:

```c
if (bs->position+nbBytes > bs->size) return 0;
```

So if `bs->position + nbBytes > bs->size`, it returns 0 without writing. But `latm_dmx_sync_frame_bs` checks `if (gf_bs_available(bs) < size) { return GF_FALSE; }`. So `size <= gf_bs_available(bs)`. And `gf_bs_available(bs)` is `bs->size - bs->position`. So `bs->position + size <= bs->size`. So `gf_bs_read_data` will write all `size` bytes.

So the WRITE happens first. The crash should be a WRITE.
